A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PROSPERO research framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational experiments across eight protein fitness landscapes, biological plausibility evaluations, noisy-surrogate robustness tests and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds distribution-shift experiments, early-round summaries and further ablation results.

M1.justification: The active learning loop, targeted alanine masking, charge-constrained EvoDiff sampling, SMC weighting and rollout selection remain unchanged. Explicitly listing the already-used coefficient k in Algorithms 2–3 clarifies their inputs; the additional variants are ablations rather than changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The eight original fitness tasks remain. Section 5.3 adds UBE2I structural-confidence optimization using pTM, with starting sequences 35 or 75 mutations from the wild-type while surrogate training uses nearby sequences. This introduces a different optimization objective and explicit distribution-shift scenarios beyond the original fitness and artificial-noise evaluations.

E2.justification: The ten external baselines and their membership in retained comparisons are unchanged. The new OOD and four-round tables reuse PEX, AdaLead, GFN-AL-δCS, LatProtRL and MLDE. CloneBO and other newly discussed methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The original ten-round protocol is retained. The new OOD study uses ESMFold pTM as the oracle, four optimization iterations, 2,624 training sequences within five mutations of wild-type, and a 200-example low-data variant. Appendix A.2 also specifies short-sequence configurations for these experiments, establishing a substantial additional evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained noise study and ablations, v2 adds explicit covariate-shift and low-data robustness tests. Appendix F tests the number of starting sequences on LGK, removes charge constraints while retaining the other components, and compares ascending, descending and random charge-class orders. Appendix D.2 extends early-round analysis beyond the existing maximum-fitness curves.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five runs, with corresponding uncertainty bands in retained figures. The added tables follow this existing practice; no changed run count, new significance testing or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: All eight original tables retain their numerical entries, including v1 Table 4 relocated as v2 Table 9. Substantial OOD, early-round and ablation results are added. For example, the new severe-shift comparison reports maximum pTM of 0.672 ± 0.031 for PROSPERO and 0.652 ± 0.059 for MLDE (Table 4); these are new-condition results, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 revises intermediate SMC targets from being 'not defined' to being 'defined only implicitly' and unavailable for direct weight computation. This is a limited correction to the mathematical rationale. Equations 1–12 remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about guided active learning, targeted masking, biologically constrained SMC, and robust fitness–novelty optimization. The additional experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking fewer starting sequences to deeper exploration and more starting sequences to greater diversity, and motivates processing constrained charge classes first. It also interprets the new OOD results as evidence of robustness to distribution shifts and data scarcity. The existing limitations and future-work discussion are retained in Appendix B.

D1.justification: v2 adds a PROSPERO code-availability link, dataset and baseline license information, initial-dataset novelty values, and construction details for the new OOD dataset. Existing surrogate-training hyperparameters, EvoDiff size, hardware and runtime disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands positioning against classifier and discrete diffusion guidance, SMC guidance and pseudo-marginal MCMC. It also develops a detailed comparison with the already-cited CloneBO, distinguishing the generative prior, weight computation and hard charge constraints. Additional citations in the main text broaden the discussion of model-based optimization and active learning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose, including the abstract and conclusion, is retained. v2 clarifies the SMC explanation and notation, makes limited wording corrections, moves the Discussion to Appendix B, and adds an appendix contents page. These are localized explanatory and organizational edits rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial tabular presentation for OOD comparisons, four-round summaries and three further ablation studies (Table 4 and Tables 10–19). The former main-text diversity table moves to Appendix D.1 as Table 9, and existing displays are rearranged. Figures 1–4 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central robustness claim: v1's dedicated robustness study used injected surrogate noise, whereas v2 also tests explicit distribution shifts and data scarcity. Appendix F tests charge constraints with the other components intact and examines additional design sensitivities. Expanded research positioning and code-access information further improve assessability. The new OOD evidence remains limited to UBE2I and predicted pTM, but it addresses an important gap in the earlier evaluation.
